chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Margaret on Harlem and celebrities she met
summary: She says she came in 1932, knew Harlem well and met Lena Horne, Lana Turner and a young Ella Fitzgerald.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's right. We had Sudan Club. I used to work with clubs. I used to get charity. We took care of the hospitals and everything. I was the treasurer of the club and everything. That's before Jay and I ever got married. I know a lot about Harlem. I can tell you more about Harlem than anybody in the world. I came here in 1932... This house, we had doormen, we had elevator men. They didn't allow you to walk up

these stairs. We had everything. But I can tell you the time I met Lena Horne. I can tell you I've met Lana Turner and I knew Ella Fitzgerald as a babe. She was only 15 years old. They don't remember me and I don't want them to remember me, 'cause I worked for a man that even gave Bob Hope his first tuxedo... I'm saying that you can meet these celebrities when they're not nothing and then when they get something they forget about you. You know what I mean? Now I knew Lena Horne down in the village, Cafe Society.
